hilfe.name: Help for the fields (expand)
hilfe.description: What the field is for, what to enter and where to get the value.

data.help_netzentgelt: Grid fee (price sheet of the grid operator)

data_description.help_netzentgelt:
**Grid fee standard stage (gross)** – Why: Grid fee outside the high and low tariff times; also the base of the dynamic tariff. Enter: ct/kWh gross (incl. VAT). Source: Grid fee price sheet of your grid operator, standard energy price.

**Grid fee low tariff (gross)** – Why: Energy price of the grid fee during the low tariff times of module 3. Enter: ct/kWh gross. Source: Price sheet for time-variable grid fees of your grid operator.

**Grid fee high tariff (gross)** – Why: Energy price of the grid fee during the high tariff times of module 3. Enter: ct/kWh gross. Source: Price sheet for time-variable grid fees of your grid operator.

**Module 1 flat rebate** – Why: Flat reduction of the grid fee for controllable consumers (module 1); a prerequisite for module 3. Enter: EUR per year gross. Source: Price sheet of your grid operator (§14a, module 1) or your notice.

**Extra base price module 3** – Why: Extra yearly cost of module 3 compared to today, e.g. a higher metering fee. Enter: EUR per year; 0 if no extra cost is known. Source: Grid operator or metering point operator.
data_description.help_tarife:
**Current energy price (gross)** – Why: Your current electricity price; the reference all savings are calculated against. Enter: Energy price in ct/kWh gross, all included (energy, grid fee, levies, taxes). Source: Your electricity bill or supply contract.

**Levies and taxes (gross)** – Why: Part of the price that does not depend on the tariff (concession fee, levies, electricity tax). Enter: Sum in ct/kWh gross. Source: Breakdown on your electricity bill or your supplier's price sheet.

**VAT** – Why: Added to the energy price of the dynamic tariff. Enter: Percent, currently 19 in Germany. Source: Legal rate or your electricity bill.

**Dynamic tariff markup (net)** – Why: Surcharge of your supplier on the spot price in the dynamic tariff. Enter: ct/kWh net. Source: Price sheet or contract of the dynamic tariff.

**Extra base fee dynamic tariff** – Why: Additional base fee of the dynamic tariff compared to today. Enter: EUR per year; 0 if equal. Source: Price sheet or contract of the dynamic tariff.

**Feed-in tariff** – Why: Revenue for exported power; also the value of surplus that stays in the battery instead of going to the grid. Enter: ct/kWh. Source: Feed-in contract, statement of the grid operator, or the applicable value under direct marketing.
data_description.help_speicher:
**Usable storage capacity (existing)** – Why: Capacity of your battery that the optimisation may use. Enter: kWh actually usable, i.e. without reserve and manufacturer limits (e.g. 15 kWh gross × 0.9). Source: Data sheet or app of your battery.

**Usable capacity of the storage expansion** – Why: Additional usable capacity of a planned expansion; used to answer whether more storage pays off. Enter: kWh usable; 0 if no expansion is planned. Source: Quote or data sheet of the expansion.

**Cost of storage expansion** – Why: Cost of the expansion; the payback time is derived from it. Enter: Euro. Source: Quote from your installer.

**Storage efficiency (charge and discharge)** – Why: Losses when charging and discharging combined. Enter: Percent (round trip), typically about 85 to 92. Source: Data sheet of the battery.

**Storage power (C-rate)** – Why: How fast the battery can charge and discharge relative to its capacity. Enter: 1/h: 0.5 means the capacity is charged or discharged in 2 hours. Maximum power in kW divided by capacity in kWh. Source: Data sheet of the battery.

**Storage wear cost** – Why: Wear of the battery per kWh charged or discharged; keeps the optimisation from needless cycles. Enter: ct/kWh; 0 is a good assumption when unsure. Source: Estimate: purchase price ÷ (cycles × capacity).
data_description.help_anschluss:
**Grid connection: maximum import power (0 = unlimited)** – Why: The battery together with the household must not draw more from the grid than the connection allows. Enter: kW; 0 = unlimited. Source: Main fuse (e.g. 3 × 35 A ≈ 24 kW) or grid connection contract.

**Grid connection: maximum export power (0 = unlimited)** – Why: The battery must not export more to the grid than allowed. Enter: kW; 0 = unlimited. Source: Plant registration or requirement of the grid operator (possibly an export limit).
